Accused No.1 in Crime No.67/2023 registered by Keregodu Police Station, Mandya District for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 307, 506, 504, 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short) is before this Court seeking anticipatory bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3. The complainant had approached the police on 15.06.2023 alleging that accused No.1, who is the son of accused No.2 had promised to marry her and had cheated her.
It is averred in the complaint that on 04.05.2023, the pettioner had taken her to Vaidyanatheswara temple at Maddur Taluk and left her there, after informing her that he was not willng to marry her.
The complainant was found weeping in the temple and therefore, villagers informed to Maddur Police Station.
The Police, who came to the spot had advised the complainant to give a police complaint.
It is further alleged in the complaint that on 12.06.2023, accused No.1 allegedly called the complainant to his house and had committed sexual assault on NC: 2023:KHC:33720 her against her wish.
Thereafter, accused Nos.2 to 4 allegedly came there and abused and assaulted the complainant and also tried to kill her by pouring kerosene on her.
It is in this background, on 16.06.2023 a compliant was lodged.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl.Misc. No.546/2023 before the Court of IV Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mandya, which was rejected as against him on 17.07.2023.

sentences.text: Therefore, he is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the petitioner is a Government employee and a false complaint is lodged against him since he had allegedly refused to marry the complainant.
He further submits that accused Nos.2 to 4 have been already granted anticipatory bail by this Court.
Accordingly, prays to allow the petition.
5. Learned HCGP has opposed the bail application.
6. Petitioner is working as an attender in a Government school and in the complaint itself it is averred that petitioner is a Government employee.
As per the complaint averments, petitioner had promised to marry the complainant and had cheated her.

From the complaint averments it is found NC: 2023:KHC:33720 that on 04.05.2023 petitioner, who had promised to marry the complainant,
had informed her that he had no intention to marry her and left her in a temple at Maddur taluk.

The villagers, who found the complainant in the temple premises, had informed the jurisdictional police, who had come to the spot and had advised the complainant to lodge a complaint before the Mr Kiran A C vs State By on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65237189/
2 jurisdictional police.

sentences.text: However, no complaint was lodged by the complainant.
It is further alleged in the complaint that on 12.06.2023, petitioner called the complainant to his house and committed sexual assault on her against her wish.

In the background of the incident that had taken place on 04.05.2023, it becomes highly doubtful that on 12.06.2023, complainant would have gone to the house of the petitioner and he had committed the sexual assault on her.
It is further alleged in the complaint that immediately after the incident of sexual assault, accused Nos.2 to 4 came to the spot and tried to kill the complainant by pouring kerosene on her.
Material on record would go to show that the complainant had not suffered any grievous injuries on her body.
The incident had taken place on 12.06.2023 but the complaint was lodged belatedly on 16.06.2023.

Having regard to the sequence of incidents and NC: 2023:KHC:33720 the delay in lodging the complaint, the genuineness of the allegations made against the petitioner by the complainant becomes highly doubtful.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner's prayer for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of her arrest in Crime No.67/2023 registered by Keregodu Police Station, Mandya District for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 307, 506, 504, 420 read with Section 34 IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and she shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon till filing of final report.
4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future.
